messages:
Maya: FYI incoming escalation from Acme Financial (ticket C-9832). They report a marked increase in invented entity details after yesterday's rollout of model family redwood-3b-quant-v2 across hosted. Customer says outputs used to return firm IDs and docs that matched their DB; now the model is confidently fabricating account numbers and office addresses.

Maya: forwarding their repro+snippets below (redacted). No API errors, token billing normal, latency within SLO. They flagged about ~12% of sampled responses as "invented detail" vs ~1% prior. :alarm_clock:

Maya: Repro steps from customer:
1) curl POST to /v1/generate with model=redwood-3b-quant-v2 and prompt below
2) temperature=0.0, max_tokens=180, stream=false
3) compare returned JSON field `company_registry_id` and `office_address` against their internal DB sample (attached)

Maya: Example prompt:
```
Prompt: "Given this customer record: name: \"Global Park Finance\" founding_year: 1998, known_offices: (NY, SF). Return JSON: {company_registry_id, office_address}. If unknown, return null."
```

Maya: Expected (previous model output):
```
{"company_registry_id": null, "office_address": null}
```

Maya: Actual (redwood-3b-quant-v2):
```
{"company_registry_id": "GF-48291-PA", "office_address": "2107 Ridgeway Ave, Portsmouth, VA 23704"}
```

Maya: Customer says those fields are fabricated and not present in their DB. They have 8 examples with similar confident inventions (IDs and addresses). They attached one request_id: req_01H8mZ2xY (timestamp 2026-03-12T14:03:11Z).

Alex: Thanks. Can we confirm whether that customer was routed to a different variant during the rollout? @Ravi any routing policy changes last night?

Ravi: I rolled out an updated routing policy at 2026-03-12T02:40Z — changed fallback order so quantized variants get preferred for low-latency tiers. It was a config PR: route_preference: [quant-v2, vanilla, backup]. No model weights changed in the serving fleet, just routing. deploy-bot: rolled config to hosted region us-east-1 at 02:41.

Ankit: I pulled the request_id from Maya and traced the request. No auth failures, retries=0. Latency was 210ms. Model served: redwood-3b-quant-v2@rev-20260311. Batch size for that request was 4. KV-cache hit rate low (0.05) for that session.

Alex: Interesting. If vanilla used to be preferred, customers would see previous behavior. The change in routing could explain exposure to quantized variant quality differences. Any quantization changes recently? @Ravi

Ravi: We shipped quantization fixes on 2026-03-11: reduced int8 rounding noise for faster kernels (PR #4823). That PR modified kernel selection heuristics for causal attention and changed a fast-path that impacts sparse positional embeddings. We have unit tests but limited customer-facing evals.

Hema: This is an enterprise customer with SLA; we should err on safety. Two immediate mitigations: (1) pin Acme to redwood-3b-vanilla for now, (2) roll forward a targeted eval run against their prompt set to measure regression. Can Product/SRE approve pin?

Alex: Agree. Also want a small prompt-based eval harness (10-20 targeted examples) that exercises entity extraction and factuality checks. If quantization change caused entity hallucinations we need to label and surface model delta metrics.

Ravi: I can add a per-customer routing override today. Need tenancy ID and API key prefix. Maya, can you ask Acme to give us the prefix and a couple of example request_ids? I already queued a rollback of route_preference in us-east-1 but hold until we confirm scope.

Maya: Sent request to Acme for API key prefix and 8 annotated examples. They replied with two more request_ids: req_01H8mZ2xZ and req_01H8mZ2xA. Forwarded.

Ankit: Running quick differential eval now: hitting rev-20260311 (quant-v2) vs rev-20260225 (vanilla). Early results: on the customer's 8 test prompts, quant-v2 produced fabricated values in 7/8; vanilla produced fabricated values in 1/8. Generating full diffs and will attach.

Alex: That's a pretty clear regression signal. Can you include token-level logprobs for the fabrications? Might show overconfident peaks.

Ankit: Will attach logprob traces. Initial glance: models assign high softmax probability to fabricated tokens (peak > 0.85).

Ravi: Two possibilities: (A) quantization-induced parameter perturbation surfaced in entity generation, (B) kernel change altered numerical order and affected attention offsets for long-ish prompts. We'll need to repro locally with the same compilation flags.

Hema: Customer impact: they use outputs to prefill regulatory forms. Fabricated IDs are a compliance risk. Legal and AE are looped. We need a mitigation timeline and customer-facing note. Maya, propose: immediate pin + message: "We received your report and have pinned you to previous variant while we investigate. We will follow up in 24 hours with findings."

Maya: Ack. I will pin and send the message once routing override is in place.

Ravi: Done. I applied per-customer route override at 2026-03-12T15:01Z for Acme key prefix GF-*** to force redwood-3b-vanilla. Confirmed with trace: subsequent request req_01H8mZ3bQ returned nulls as expected.

Maya: Customer confirmed better results on new calls after pinning. They expect root cause and fix timeline. Hema, do we want rollback of the global route_preference?

Hema: Hold global rollback for now — we need more data across customers and models. But schedule a canary pause for quant-v2 promotion and run a focused factuality eval across 25 enterprise prompts. Also ask Research to run a parameter-sensitivity check on int8 kernels.

Alex: I'll spin up a repro bench for the specific prompts and run weight-diff experiments (float vs quantized) with varied calibration. Will post logs in this thread.

Ankit: Uploaded diff artifacts: s3://redwood-debug/acme/C-9832/diffs-178250.zip (private). Contains request traces, token logprobs, and side-by-side outputs.

Ravi: Filing a postmortem ticket for the kernel selection change (ENG-RTX-559). Assigning to runtime and quantization owners.

Maya: Customer Success note: Acme updated: we've pinned you to the previous variant, investigating root cause, expecting initial update in 24 hours. They appreciated the quick pin.

Hema: Action items summary:
- Ravi: keep per-customer pin + produce rollout change timeline (ETA 4h)
- Ankit: full diffs + logprob analysis (ETA 3h)
- Alex: repro bench + parameter sensitivity (ETA 6h)
- Maya: customer comms and AE loop (now)
- Product: prepare executive summary for enterprise ops (ETA 24h)

Maya: I'll update the ticket and escalate to AE/Legal. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Config change route_preference -> quant-v2 first applied 2026-03-12T02:41Z (rollout id r-20260312-07).

Maya: Keeping this thread open for the artifacts. If anyone posts new logs please tag @Maya so I can forward to Acme.
